- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a 1–2 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.33) and news volume drops, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.3–0.8% to avoid mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment change is volatile (e.g., >1.0 in consecutive days), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in high-news periods; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias if news volume >2.5 for 3+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is flat (±0.33) and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5% per day until sentiment shifts.
